text:
maya: heads up — bringing up the new hf/gpt-mid model hit a weird token mismatch. fast loader uses tokenizer.json (sha256:aaa111...) but slow/py-tokenizer reads tokenizer_config.json (sha256:bbb222...) and the chat template explodes. :face_with_monocle:

alex: ugh. is it the file missing or different fields? can you paste the diffs?

maya: not a missing file — both present. diff looks like the `special_tokens` object is present in tokenizer.json but flattened/renamed in tokenizer_config.json -> causes fast vs slow mapping to disagree. quick dump below:

maya: ```
# tokenizer.json snippet (fast)
"special_tokens": {"bos_token": "", "eos_token": "", "pad_token": "<|pad|>"}

# tokenizer_config.json (slow)
"special_tokens": [{"name": "bos_token", "id": 1, "content": ""}, {"name": "pad_token", "id": 2, "content": "<|pad|>"}]
```

priya: that format mismatch is classic HF export variance. did the HF side produce both artifacts from the same commit? could be an old `tokenizer_config` from the converter script.

sam: repro steps i used: `huggingface-cli download --repo my/model && ls -la` then `redwood-convert --input ./model --output ./artifacts` . converter logs show fallback to `tokenizer_config` when `tokenizer.json` checksum doesn't match expected. log snippet:

sam: ```
[2026-03-19 14:02:01] converter INFO: found tokenizer.json (sha=aaa111)
[2026-03-19 14:02:01] converter WARN: tokenizer.json checksum != model.meta.tokenizer_sha -> using tokenizer_config.json (sha=bbb222)
[2026-03-19 14:02:01] runtime ERROR: chat template resolution failed: missing <|bos|> mapping
```

maya: exactly. looks like the model package had two tokenizers from different pipeline stages. fast runtime happily used tokenizer.json mapping, but the slow loader sees the mismatch and falls back — which ends up with inconsistent token ids and eval regressions (qa-f1 drop ~4.7 pts).

alex: any quick mitigation? force converter to prefer tokenizer.json if present and warn instead of switching? or canonicalize both formats during conversion?

priya: we should canonicalize. propose: conversion step verify both digests; if mismatch, run a reconciliation pass that maps `special_tokens` entries into the same canonical shape (prefer the `tokenizer.json` mapping since that’s what fast runtime uses) and write out a reconciled `tokenizer_config.json` and update metadata token_sha. Also emit a warning + link to the offending HF commit.

maya: +1. also add a small eval smoke test in onboarding: run a short prompt set (10 prompts) and compare embedding similarity / sequence ids to catch id map shifts early.

sam: i'll prototype a script `reconcile_tokenizers.py` that loads both formats and emits a canonical `tokenizer_config.json`. sample logic below:

sam: ```py
# pseudo
def reconcile(fast_json, slow_config):
    # build name->id map from slow_config list
    # build name->token from fast_json special_tokens map
    # if ids conflict, remap ids in slow_config to match fast_json ordering
    # write reconciled config and update model.meta.tokenizer_sha = sha256(new_tokenizer_config)
```

tokenizer-bot: artifact check: uploaded artifacts/model-v2/tokenizer.json sha256=aaa111, tokenizer_config.json sha256=bbb222. created reconciliation ticket #ML-459.

infra-bot: note: if we change token_sha in metadata, downstream dedicated caches must be invalidated — will add invalidation hook to deploy pipeline.

alex: timeline?

priya: sam -> 1 day prototype. if tests pass, we can roll to staging and re-run quantization experiments (we saw 6% perf improvement earlier but worried regressed quality was due to mapping).

maya: thanks all. adding checklist: 1) reconcile script, 2) onboarding smoke eval, 3) converter warns + link, 4) cache invalidation hook. tagging @sam to follow up. :thumbsup:
